Your entire response must be the JSON object itself, starting with { and ending with }, parseable by JSON.parse(). No zip export yet. - Credits: metered from real AI cost. A build that fails to compile is never charged. - Free tier: 750 credits on signup, no credit card required. - Every publish is scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets/API keys before going live. What Kodely does NOT do yet — never claim these (the brief below wrongly says "yours to keep" and "first month of hosting free" and references a non-existent "Agency plan" — correct all of this): - No backend, database, auth, or payments generation. Frontend only — be direct that this is exactly why it's good for FRONTEND prototyping specifically, not full-stack prototyping. - No custom domains. Only *.kodely.site subdomains today. - No code export/download (zip). "Yours to keep" is misleading — the honest claim is "you can see and copy the code" in-app; there's no export, which matters for a developer who might want to pull the code into their own repo — be upfront this isn't possible as a one-click action yet. - No click-to-edit visual editing. { "slug": "ai-website-builder-for-developers-fast-prototyping", "title": "Kodely for Developers: Fast Frontend Prototyping", "metaTitle": "Kodely for Developers: Fast Frontend Prototyping", "metaDescription": "Kodely generates real React and TypeScript components from a chat prompt, so you can scaffold a frontend prototype in minutes instead of hand-coding it.", "targetKeyword": "ai website builder for developers", "category": "Personas", "bodyHtml": "

You already know how to build a frontend. That is not the problem Kodely solves. The problem is time: a client demo due tomorrow, a hackathon UI you need working by 6pm, a design direction you want to see rendered before you commit two days to hand-building it. You could code any of these yourself. Describing them in a chat prompt and getting a working first pass is just faster, especially for UI you are not precious about and expect to iterate on anyway.

How Kodely actually fits into that workflow

Kodely is not a mockup generator and it is not a black box. When you describe a page or a flow, it generates a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app — actual .tsx component files, not raw HTML glued together and not a design tool export. You get a live preview of the compiled app as it is built, and a code view where you can read the actual generated source and judge it the way you would judge a pull request. If the component structure is off, you will see it. If the Tailwind classes are sloppy, you will see that too. Nothing here asks you to trust the output on faith.

Iteration works the same way it started: you describe the change in chat and Kodely edits the real components, not a static screenshot of them. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so rolling back a change that did not work is free and instant — no git gymnastics required for a throwaway prototype.

Where this is genuinely useful

  • Client-facing demos. You need something clickable and credible for a pitch, not a Figma frame someone has to imagine as software. Describe the flow, get a real running app on a public URL, send the link.
  • Hackathons. The frontend is rarely the interesting part of a hackathon idea, but it still has to exist and it still eats hours. Scaffold it in chat and spend your remaining time on whatever your project actually differentiates on.
  • Validating a design direction. Before you hand-build a layout, generate two or three variations and look at them running in a browser. It is a much better gut check than a static comp, and far cheaper than building each one yourself to find out which works.

The honest limits

This matters more to a developer than to anyone else, so we are not going to soften it.

  • No export yet. You can see and copy the generated code in-app, but there is no one-click zip download or repo push. If your plan is to pull the output into your own codebase, you will be copying files by hand today — that is a real gap if you were hoping to treat this as a scaffolding step for production work.
  • Frontend only. No backend, no database, no auth, no payments. Kodely generates the UI layer and nothing underneath it. That is by design: it is a frontend prototyping tool, not a full-stack app generator, and it is honest about that boundary rather than faking a backend you would have to rip out later.
  • No custom domains. Published sites live at a <name>.kodely.site subdomain. There is no custom domain support yet.
  • Chat-based editing only. There is no click-to-edit visual canvas. Changes go through the same chat interface you used to generate the app.

Pricing, in plain terms

There is one plan. Everyone gets 750 free credits on signup, no credit card required, and credits are metered from the actual AI cost of each generation. If a build fails to compile, you are not charged for it. There is no tier system and no separate agency plan — pricing is the same for every account. Full details are on the pricing page.

One more thing worth knowing before you publish anything: every deployed site is scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, which matters if you are the kind of developer who pastes an example key into a prompt and forgets about it.

Try it on something real

The fastest way to know if this fits your workflow is to point it at an actual prototype you need this week — a demo, a hackathon screen, a layout you are trying to decide on. See what it generates and read the code it hands you.

Start building free — no credit card required. You can also see more of how it works on the homepage or browse the blog for more build breakdowns.
